headline: Approved transferring $1.3 million to the City of Gloucester and other library business
summary: The Board approved a $1.3 million transfer from the BankGloucester Building Account to the City of Gloucester, with $490,000 for interest and $810,000 for principal. The Board also approved notifying the City that final project costs total $27,483,468, accepted the Treasurer's Report, approved Teen Room modifications costing $19,700, and added Katy Marques to the Board.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 28, 2026 meeting as amended, via roll call, with Peter L, Jen, and John abstaining.
Approved authorizing the Treasurer to transfer $1.3m from the BankGloucester Building Account to the City of Gloucester, including $490,000 interest and $810,000 principal, via roll call.
Approved authorizing the Board Treasurer to notify the City of Gloucester Treasurer that final project costs will be $27,483,468, reducing the prior $29m figure by $1,516,532, via roll call.
Approved accepting the Treasurer's Report as presented, via roll call.
Approved authorizing Jenny to proceed with the $19,700 Teen Room rearrangement plan as presented, via roll call.
Approved accepting Katy Marques to the Board of the Library, via roll call.

Gloucester Lyceum & Sawyer Free Library 
Board of Trustees 
Meeting Minutes 
Tuesday, August 25, 2026 at 5:30 pm  
Sawyer Free Library Conference Room 
2 Dale Avenue, Gloucester, MA 
As the recent amendments to the open meeting law allows, this committee will continue to hold 
meetings remotely. Adequate alternative access to the meeting is provided through the zoom link 
below. 
And via ZOOM : https://us02web.zoom.us/j/85276115907 
 
Attendance: in person: Fran Aliberte, Christine Araujo, Geoff Bradford, Peter Brau, John Day, Steven 
Lewis, Jeremy Melvin (joined at 5:35), Kathleen Reynolds, Dawn Sarrouf, Leora Ulrich, Library 
Director Jenny Benedict, and guest Mayor Paul Lundberg (left at 6:18) 
Via video conference: Jason Brisbois, Rick Ciolino, Joe Grella, Jen Holmgren, Peter Lawrence, 
 
Not Present: Cheryl Marks 
 
1. Call to order 
 
2. Welcome and introductions 
a. Peter B moved to welcome Jason, Rick, Joe, Jen, and Peter L into the meeting. Fran 
seconded and the motion was approved via roll call.  
 
3. Approval of minutes from July 28, 2026. Peter B offered corrections. Fran moved to approve the 
minutes as amended and Leora seconded. Peter L, Jen, and John abstained and the minutes were 
approved via roll call.  
 
4. Treasurer’s Report – Joe 
a. The audit is on-going. Joe will present reports on the first few months of the fiscal year 
once the audit is complete. 
b. Investments: Though we withdrew interest and dividends totaling ~$20,000; the value of 
our investments remains constant. 
 
5. Transfer to the City 
a. The Executive Committee voted to recommend the Corporation transfer $1.3m to the 
City; of that $490,000 will be applied to interest.  
b. Joe moved to authorize the Treasurer to transfer $1.3m from the BankGloucester Building 
Account to the City of Gloucester. This transfer will include $490,000 of interest and 
$810,000 of principal. This payment falls within the Library FY2027 budget of $1m 
principal and $500,000 interest. Jen seconded and the motion was approved via roll call. 
Joe will initiate the transfer tomorrow.  
c. Joe moved to authorize the Board Treasurer to notify the City of Gloucester Treasurer that 
final project costs will be $27,483,468. Future BANs will be based on this number, not the 
original $29m (a reduction of $1,516,532). Jen seconded and the motion was approved via 
roll call.  
d. Joe reported on balances with the City. After this transfer we will have paid ~$15.7m in 
principal to the City leaving a balance due of $11,831,144. We will have paid $862,791 in 
interest.
Page 2 of 4 
 
e. Peter B moved to accept the Treasurer’s Report as presented. Dawn seconded and the 
Report was approved via roll call.  
 
6. Fundraising Update – See Corporate Communications below 
 
7. ARIS Report – Jenny 
a. We just passed our one-year anniversary of being back in the building. Jenny commended 
the staff for their hard work.  
b. Jenny shared an update on numbers of visitors and circulation. Circulation and foot traffic 
have increased about 30%. Electronic materials have increased about 13% over last year 
and doubled over numbers from four years ago. We have just over 11,000 card-holders – 
up about 2,000 in the past year; staff register about 200 new cards every month. 
c. Programming: Staff have curated a diverse range of programs. Participation at all age 
levels of programming is up.  
d. Meeting Room use: The meeting rooms were used 492 times in FY2026. The software 
registration program has been useful. 
e. Public-use computers and internet: Use is up about 45%.  
f. Staffing: In addition to paid staff we had ten volunteers and seven interns. Through 
donations we are able to increase youth services, early learning staff, and digital services 
person in FY2027. 
g. Friends of the Library: The Friends have disbanded since the move. Which means we no 
longer have the book sale. Another role they played was providing hospitality (snacks, 
etc.) for events.  
h. Jenny thanked the Board for their support through the year. Geoff thanked Jenny for 
compiling the data.  
 
8. Teen Room Modifications – Geoff 
a. Teen Room staff have requested more office space in the Teen Room. Jenny suggests 
using surplus state funds to finance modifications to the space. Specifically, moving the 
circulation desk to the opposite side of the entry and converting the freed-up space to 
office space. 
b. The Executive Committee reviewed two possible solutions and voted to recommend 
moving forward with the less expensive $19,700 option. 
c. Discussion: Existing furniture and stacks can be shifted around so the teens will not lose 
floor space. Jenny shared drawings and a visual representation of what to expect. There is 
a six-week lead time to receive the necessary pieces; making the change will take one day.  
d. Peter B moved to authorize Jenny to proceed with the plan as presented. Dawn seconded 
and the motion was approved via roll call.  
 
9. Committee Reports 
a. Corporate Communications – Fran 
i. Board recruitment: Fran and John met with Katy Marques. They were impressed with 
her background and experience. Kathleen moved to accept Katy to the Board of the 
Library. Peter L seconded and the motion was approved via roll call.  
ii. Art Auction September 18: Christine is looking for volunteers for September 17 to help 
with set up.  
iii. Fundraising: Donations for the current fiscal year to date total ~$100,000. Our goal for 
the year is $1.6m. John suggests the Board create a structure to support fundraising 
efforts.  
iv. Grant Writer: We would like to hire a part-time grant writer to research family 
foundations.
Page 3 of 4 
 
v. Christine Araujo is the newest member of Corporate Communications.  
b. Saunders House – Geoff 
i. Structural reinforcement: Replacement of the fire suppression system will begin soon. 
ii. Middle Street Door: The old door has been removed; the new door is yet to be 
installed.  
iii. Grant Opportunity: Jenny submitted an application for a tourism grant for Saunders 
House and the murals.  
c. Building & Grounds – Peter L 
i. Peter L walked the grounds with Michael Byrne, head of the Patio Company. They 
recently did some pruning and removed non-native plants growing in the native plant 
garden. The fountain is functioning well. They are getting familiar with the irrigation 
system and watering needs. Plants will be replaced where necessary in the spring. 
ii. Peter L will meet with Lisa from G2 to brainstorm ideas for Saunders House grounds.  
iii. Railings: Jenny is working with WT Rich and the manufacturers to address 
discoloration on the railings. 
iv. The Patio Company will recommend a salt substitute for winter that will be easier on 
the plants.  
v. Saunders House: there was some confusion on whether or not Saunders House 
grounds were part of the original contract. That has been clarified and work is on-
going.  
vi. Solar: The panels have been installed and have been inspected. National Grid will 
install a special meter and then the system will be turned on. When Jenny has access 
to the dashboard she will share that with the Committee.  
d. Lyceum – Steven  
i. Bylaws update: The Lyceum Committee approved updates to their bylaws. Geoff 
presented it to the Board for review. He asked that Trustees review the document and 
be prepared to discuss it at the September meeting.  
• Discussion: We need clarification on the Committee versus the Lyceum 
“community” in the document.  
ii. Coming Up: 
• Fall: A panel discussion on AI. They have secured a moderator and two panelists. 
• Spring: Celebration of Democracy 
 
10. Annual Meeting: The meeting is scheduled for Wednesday November 11. Fran will have information 
on deadlines for inclusion on the agenda.  
 
11. Next Meeting: September 22, 2026 
 
12. 7:00 Adjourn. There being no further business the meeting was adjourned. 
 
Respectfully submitted, Tracy Bowen 
 
Motions Summary 
Joe moved to authorize the Treasurer to transfer $1.3m from the BankGloucester Building Account to 
the City of Gloucester. Jen seconded and the motion was approved via roll call.  
 
Joe moved to authorize the Board Treasurer to notify the City of Gloucester Treasurer that final project 
costs will be $27,483,468. Future BANs will be based on this number, not the original $29m (a reduction 
of $1,516,532). Jen seconded and the motion was approved via roll call.  
 
Peter B moved to accept the Treasurer’s Report as presented. Dawn seconded and the Report was

approved via roll call.  
 
Peter B moved to authorize Jenny to proceed with the plan to rearrange the Teen Room as presented. 
Dawn seconded and the motion was approved via roll call.  
 
Kathleen moved to accept Katy Marques to the Board of the Library. Peter L seconded and the motion 
was approved via roll call.  
 
 
Actions Summary 
Joe will initiate the $1.3m transfer to the City tomorrow.  
 
Geoff asked that Trustees review the proposed Lyceum Bylaws and be prepared to discuss it at the 
September meeting.
